boardTitle: B168 and DT349: the recipe's header is the whole meal, the Plate's PD card, the portions to cook as chips in Foods

B168.title: The numbers under One portion show the whole recipe

opportunity.from: Seen while drawing B166, 23 November 2026, on Lazy Burek's page; Coach Milan 24 November 07:04: yes, its own ticket, we need to fix that.
opportunity.job: Read what one portion of my recipe holds.
opportunity.kind: Says something not true: the table under One portion shows the whole recipe.
opportunity.why_now: B166 made the table readable, so its numbers are now read.

B168.problem: On a recipe that makes 4 portions, the PD card says One portion, 549 kcal and 224 g. Its numbers say Total 897 g and 2,194 kcal, fat 135 g: the whole recipe. The Nutrition table below says 1 portion, 224 g. Two places on one page disagree about one portion.
B168.story: When I read a recipe's PD card and its numbers, I want them to say the same meal, so that I can trust what I plan and eat.
B168.now: The card says One portion, 549 kcal · 23.3 g protein · 224 g. Its numbers are handed the whole recipe: Total 897 g, 2,194 kcal. Cook it's − 4 portions + sits under the card and changes only the foods to cook.
B168.proposed: The PD card is the whole meal, as the recipe makes it: its title says All 4 portions, its rows 2,194 kcal, 897 g, 93 g, and its numbers Total 897 g and 2,194 kcal. One portion and 100 g stay in the Nutrition table, side by side with the whole recipe, for comparison. The portions to cook do not change the header (DT349).
B168.looked_at: The card at one portion (07:10): not chosen, 14:50: the header is the whole meal. − and + inside the card (07:55): not chosen, no more navigation in the card. The card following Cook it (08:05): not chosen; reading would change the batch. Numbers for above the card (14:00): not chosen, 14:49: the header is the meal; portioning goes somewhere else.
B168.short: The PD card and its numbers are the whole meal, as the recipe makes it; with DT349 in one release, 0.3.193

DT349.title: The recipe's header: the Plate's PD card, a placeholder photo with its buttons, the portions to cook as chips in Foods

opportunity.from: Coach Milan 24 November 2026, 07:42, looking at the board B168; 13:44 to 14:50, brainstorm on the header and the portions.
opportunity.job: Read a recipe's numbers the way I read a plate, and cook the batch I choose.
opportunity.kind: Did not find it or did not understand it: the recipe's PD card looks different from the Plate's; Cook it looks like a button and sits by the numbers, which it does not change.
opportunity.why_now: B168 makes the card count a chosen number of portions, so the card and the cooking need their own places.

DT349.problem: The recipe page's PD card has its own layout: one small line for kcal, protein and grams, its numbers inside the card. On the Plate the same card has rows and opens its numbers under it. Cook it, under the card, looks like a call to action and says 1 portions.
DT349.story: When I open a recipe, I want its header to show the meal the way the Plate shows a plate, and to choose how much I cook where the foods are, so that I find each in its place.
DT349.now: Recipe page: title, a No photo yet card with two buttons, the PD card (own layout: one small line, numbers inside), a Cook it card with − 4 portions + that looks like a button and says 1 portions, Foods, Nutrition, Steps with Start cooking.
DT349.proposed: 1. The header is the meal: title, photo, PD card, Nutrition (14:49). 2. No photo yet: a placeholder picture of a meal in the photo's place, with No photo yet, Let Chef Mealan draw one and Add my photo on it. 3. The PD card is the Plate's card, one component (PdCard): PD with its tap to the scale, the words against your target, Energy, Weight and Protein as rows, the letters; the numbers open under the card. 4. Cook for, at the top of Foods: chips 1 to 5 for the usual cases (one person, a couple or two meals, a family of 3, 4 or 5; Coach Milan 15:14), the recipe's own number marked as written, the plan's number when it has one, and Other, which opens − and + for an exact number (17:38: we need both). One tap; saved with the recipe; the grams follow; Start cooking cooks it. 1 portion, not 1 portions. The Cook it card goes. 5. docs/rules/design.md D8: every PD card is PdCard and opens its numbers under it; design-rules.cjs checks it.
DT349.looked_at: Only − and +: not chosen; three taps from 4 to 1, every time. Only chips: not chosen, 17:38: an exact number is needed too (Other). The portions to cook above the PD card (14:00): not chosen, the header is the meal. The portions at Start cooking: not chosen, far from the foods they change. Each person's own portion (a father, a mother, a kid of 10, a kid of 3): later, its own ticket, DT350 (17:38). A food's PD card (FoodCard): not in DT349, unless Coach Milan says.
DT349.short: The recipe's header: the Plate's PD card (PdCard, D8), a placeholder photo with its buttons; the portions to cook as chips in Foods; with B168, 0.3.193
